h: The Eternal Menorah Illuminates the Oral Torah

p: "Speak to Aharon and say to him:
toward the face of the Menorah
shall the seven lamps give light" (Bamidbar 8:2).
And Rashi explained, from the Sifrei,
that all of them should face the middle one,
which is on the body of the Menorah.
According to this it must be understood:
"to make known the praise of Aharon,
one must understand what praise it is
that he did not deviate from Hashem's command
And in Midrash Rabbah (beginning of this parshah, Bamidbar Rabbah 15:1):
וַיִּשְׁמַע אֶת הַקּוֹל מִדַּבֵּר וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר ז, פט)
'And he heard the Voice speaking,' etc. (Bamidbar 7:89);
what did He speak to him?
the matter of lighting the Menorah
is that it be "Come and give Me light,"
the light of the Oral Torah
And as soon as the Mishkan was erected,
and there was the place of the Shechinah's dwelling,
which is the attribute of Malchus
"For from Zion shall go forth Torah," etc.
And the essence of the Oral Torah
was in the Chamber of Hewn Stone
"And you shall arise and go up," etc.
And about this it is written
is the aspect of the Written Torah,
because they are of the Torah;
and this refers to the mitzvah itself
which is from the Written Torah;
therefore it said it with the term dibbur.
is the aspect of the Oral Torah:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג פח, ב)
which is the dew of Atika,
the aspect of the Oral Torah
would impart to Aharon the Kohen
that he be able to kindle the lamps
so that through lighting the lamps
"For the lips of the Kohen guard knowledge,
and they seek Torah from his mouth."
And this is what is said:
toward the face of the Menorah
shall the seven lamps give light":
which correspond to the seven lower attributes;
and as written in Midrash Rabbah
that the seven lamps correspond to the seven planets;
and the seven days are the seven attributes;
as written in the holy Zohar
and it does not say "in six";
which corresponds to the attribute of Malchus.
And this is what it said:
which correspond to the seven attributes,
shall give light toward the one standing
which corresponds to the Shabbos day;
and as the holy Ari reckoned:
ג׳ יָמִים דְּקַמֵּי שַׁבְּתָא ד׳ ה׳ ו׳
the three days before Shabbos, the fourth, fifth and sixth,
from the holiness of the coming Shabbos;
וְג׳ יָמִים דְּבָתַר שַׁבְּתָא א׳ ב׳ ג׳
and in the three days after Shabbos, the first, second and third,
there remains an impression of holiness
from the Shabbos that has passed;
and Shabbos is the middle one.
And therefore the attribute of Malchus is called
as written in the holy Zohar,
for it includes the holiness of all seven attributes;
and as written in the holy Zohar,
that Shabbos is the sum of all blessings;
and this is what is written:
"He blessed it above all the days,"
for there is included in Shabbos
בִּרְכַּת כָּל הַו׳ מִדּוֹת גַּם כֵּן
the blessing of all six attributes as well.
And this is what it said,
and likewise the three western ones
for all of them are included in the middle one,
which corresponds to the Shabbos day,

p: וְעַל זֶה אָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And about this Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, told
to receive the light of the Oral Torah
and stands facing the holiness of Shabbos
the attribute of Malchus, Bas Sheva,
which is comprised of all seven lamps.
to tell the praise of Aharon,
on the intention of his heart in the lighting,
the aspect of the Oral Torah,
toward the face of the Menorah,
ready to receive the holiness of
the aspect of the Oral Torah
which is called "toward the face of the Menorah,"
And this is what is said (Bamidbar 8:3):
that is, that he did it
the aspect of the Oral Torah,
toward the face of the Menorah,
And this is what it says in the Sifrei:
"To make known the praise of Aharon,
that just as Moshe told him,
And according to this will be understood
what is written in Midrash Rabbah (Bamidbar Rabbah 15:6):
except for the Nasi of Levi," etc.,
"the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him:
you are prepared for greater than this," etc.:
as long as the Beis HaMikdash stands,
'toward the face of the Menorah shall they give light';
and all the blessings that I gave you
רַק כָּל זְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
only as long as the Beis HaMikdash stands;
true, the mitzvah of Birkas Kohanim
but what does it have to do
But according to what has been said,
this is what He told him:
"you are prepared for greater than this," etc.;
the light of the Oral Torah.
And this is why the Midrash Rabbah was precise:
toward the face of the Menorah shall they give light,"
that its meaning is that they will give light
who stands toward the face of the Menorah
the light of the Oral Torah;
remains for Aharon and his sons forever.
But so that he not ask:
there will be no lighting of the lamps,
and through what will he impart
the light of the Oral Torah?
the Kohanim will impart to Yisrael
the light of the Oral Torah.
with what is his power and his level,
and Aharon's power is the Oral Torah,
"For the lips of the Kohen," etc.,
"and they seek Torah from his mouth";
therefore his blessing "May Hashem bless you"
and the essential meaning of blessing
like the blessing of the fish
as written in the holy Zohar
is increase in the Oral Torah.
is with the blessing spelled out
that is, with the light of Torah
"For a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light."
בְּרָכָה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן עַל תּוֹרָה
this blessing too is about Torah
"Hashem will give strength to His people;
Hashem will bless His people with peace."
And this is the Oral Torah,
for the essence of the Oral Torah
which is the level of Yosef,
"And they do not move from there
until they become friends of one another,
of Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel,
and truth and peace are one,
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 12b):
are bound one with the other."
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, told Aharon:
the power will remain with him forever
to impart words of Torah to Yisrael.
which corresponds to the face of the Menorah,
which is the parshah of lighting the Menorah
toward the face of the Menorah,
with a true seeking in the heart,
the aspect of the light of the Oral Torah.
